en: make a cream with pasta water

does: Binds fat, egg and a hard cheese into one glossy cream with hot starchy water, off the heat. No fat is whisked in drop by drop: the starch in the water and the warmth of the pasta hold it together, and it splits or scrambles if the heat comes back.
how: Have everything ready before the pasta is done: the fat in the pan, the egg and cheese mixed in a bowl, and a mug of hot starchy cooking water.
Take the pan off the heat. Heat is what splits this kind of sauce.
Loosen the egg and cheese with a splash of the hot water, stirring, until it is a smooth pourable cream with no streaks.
Bring it together with the fat and the pasta, adding more water a splash at a time and tossing, until it turns glossy and clings.
Serve at once. It is at its best straight away and sets as it cools.

cues.text: A smooth, glossy cream that coats the back of a spoon, with no lumps of cooked egg and no puddle of oil.
It flows like thin cream and clings to the pasta as it is tossed.
The pan has stopped sizzling before the egg goes in.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving the pan on the heat, so that the egg scrambles into flecks.
mistakes.fix: Take the pan off the heat before the egg goes in, and keep it off.

mistakes.mistake: Using water that has gone cool or has no starch, so that the sauce stays thin and slides off.
mistakes.fix: Use hot water from the pasta pot, and add it a splash at a time.

mistakes.mistake: Adding all the water at once, so that the sauce turns watery.
mistakes.fix: Add it a splash at a time and stop when it is glossy.

comes_after.why: The starchy water that binds the sauce comes from cooking the pasta.

variant_of.differs: No fat is added drop by drop. The sauce is bound with hot starchy water, off the heat, and it splits or scrambles if the heat returns.
